newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: IMPORT PRESSURE WEAKENS ZIMBABWE DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: IMPORT PRESSURE WEAKENS ZIMBABWE DOLLAR.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed one-and-a-half cents weaker on the key U.S. unit on Wednesday, weighed down by importer demand for foreign currency which was ill-matched by export inflows, dealers said.
"The market is still quite short (from the central bank's Tuesday intervention). The inflows we had today were rather tiny and all swallowed up by demand and to cover shortages," one dealer said.
The local unit finished the day at 11.3450/3550 against the U.S. dollar, dropping from Tuesday's 11.3300/3400.

On the crosses, it was quoted slightly firmer on pound sterling at 18.8800/9100 compared to 18.9075/9150 the previous day, though it was weaker compared to 18.8770/9005 in the morning. Against the mark it eased to 6.5850/5950 from 6.5675/5795 and to 2.5170/5210 versus the rand from 2.5090/5195.
